subject: Packaging options for renewal + constrained burst needs
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging inquiry: upcoming renewal and burst needs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — our renewal is up end of June and we need to lock in packaging/committed capacity. A few specifics from our side:
- Average usage: ~120 qps for embeddings + generation, peaks up to 400 qps for scheduled nightly jobs.
- Latency SLO: 200ms p50 for most product paths, a couple of high-priority flows need sub-150ms p50.
- Security: SOC 2 in place; we need audit log retention and private deployment options on the table.
- Budget: we can consider a 12–24 month committed option but need price protection for stepdowns if usage falls.

Can you share recommended packaging options that balance reserved capacity for predictable throughput and a metered overlay for spikes? Also curious how credits for migration or pilot discounts might look. I've attached a short usage snapshot and our PO template.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Park
Head of Platform Integrations | Clearline Health

Attachment: Clearline_Multiprod_Pricing_v1.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging inquiry: upcoming renewal and burst needs

Hi Emma — great context, thanks. High level recommendations below; attaching a compact matrix for visibility (redwood_pack_matrix.xlsx).

1) Balanced (Recommended) — 12m commit
- Reserved pool sized for your p95 baseline (~160 qps equivalent).
- Metered overlay for bursts to 4x baseline with pay-as-you-go tokens.
- Includes prefix/KV caching and burst cache credits that reduce token cost for repeat traffic.
- Step-down protection: automatic 3-month grace window on tier reductions.

2) Throughput Plus — 24m commit, predictable SLA
- Larger reserved capacity to cover ~300 qps sustained.
- Lower per-token cost, dedicated GPU pools for your high-priority flows (helps meet sub-150ms p50).
- Includes 2 pilot months at a 25% discount to validate production workload.

3) Compact Plus — Meter-first with committed discount
- Prize for teams looking to minimize committed spend; low base commit + higher metered ceiling.
- Good if you expect variability and prefer smaller upfront.

Migration & credits
- We can offer a one-time migration credit to offset sandbox & integration costs (typically $10–25k depending on committed tier).
- For pilot: 60–90 day pilot with a blended discounted rate and a conversion credit applied to the first invoice upon commitment.

Next steps
- If you share target commitment window and a rough committed $ amount, we’ll produce a pro-forma comparing the three options and a doc with step-down guardrails. I cc'd Ben to outline burst SLA details and Marissa for discount/negotiation path.

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_pack_matrix.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearlinehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging inquiry: upcoming renewal and burst needs

Emma — quick note on burst mechanics and SLA behavior:
- Dedicated pools (Throughput Plus) guarantee capacity and give you the lowest tail latency; they also support pre-warm windows for scheduled spikes.
- For Balanced, we overlay a metered burst layer that auto-fills when reserved capacity saturates; bursts are throttled at sustained high usage but smoothed via burst credits.
- If you have nightly jobs that spike to 400 qps, we recommend a short daily scheduled pre-warm (we can automate with cron-like rules) or a small reserved uplift to cover predictable spikes.

Operational items I recommend we include in the proposal:
- Canary rollout plan (1% -> 10% -> 50%) for any model/quantization changes
- Explicit rollback window and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if latency regresses
- Audit-log retention SLA (we can map retention days to pricing tiers)

I linked the HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789123

Ben
Principal Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma@clearlinehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging inquiry: upcoming renewal and burst needs

Emma — thanks for the detail. From a commercial perspective, a few negotiation levers that tend to matter for accounts with predictable but spiky patterns: 
- Commitment ladder: tiered discounts at $X, $Y, $Z commit bands; faster step-down protection (90 days) for the first year only.
- Pilot conversion credit: if you commit within 30 days of pilot close we apply a conversion credit equal to 40% of pilot spend (capped).
- Feature bundling: include one complimentary model quantization consultation + 1 quota of Dedicated pre-warm windows in the Throughput Plus package for 12m deals.

Proposed ask from Clearline to make the exec approval smooth:
1) 12 month Balanced agreement sized at ~$75k/month with a 10% first-year discount and 60-day step-down protection.
2) 90-day pilot at 50% list for the high-priority flows with conversion credit as above.
3) Include audit-log retention 365 days as part of the Core features.

If that looks reasonable I can draft a formal pro-forma and an amendment template for the PO. I can also include DocuSign routing to speed procurement.

Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
